equity_bridge.note: Q3-2026 10-Q Note 12: additional payment of up to $1.3bn depending on the Federal Circuit appeal; company deems loss not probable

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: scenario build (base-case 10-year revenue CAGR); no historical series is usable
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: History is a pandemic boom-bust: revenue went 803 (FY2020) -> 19,263 (FY2022) -> 1,944 (FY2025). The 3-year and 5-year CAGRs point in opposite directions, EPS and owner FCF are negative at both ends (CAGR undefined), and equity is falling with losses. None of them is a forecast basis.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF (reported FCF - SBC - interest income) was approx. -4,551 FY2023, -4,909 FY2024, -2,863 FY2025, -2,786 TTM Sep-2026 (the last including the $950m settlement; ~-1,836 excluding it). SBC has grown every year (226 FY2022 -> 483 FY2025) while revenue fell 90%: SBC is now ~19% of revenue.

scenario_narratives.base: Intismeran plus KEYTRUDA is approved in adjuvant melanoma on the INTerpath-001 result (RFS HR 0.58) and launches in 2028, and at least one of the three Phase 3 NSCLC trials reads out positively, taking end-market sales to ~$14bn by 2036 of which Moderna books half under the Merck profit share. The respiratory franchise (Spikevax, mNEXSPIKE, mRESVIA, mFLUSIVA, the flu+COVID combination ex-US) grows from ~$2.5bn to ~$4.5bn on the flu launch and the UK/Canada/Australia supply partnerships, while US COVID volumes stay under policy pressure. Costs follow the stated reduction programme through 2027, then rebuild around oncology; owner FCF turns positive in year 4 and the ~$8bn of cash and investments comfortably funds ~$2.7bn of cumulative burn before then.
scenario_narratives.bull: The melanoma result generalises: NSCLC, renal and bladder adjuvant trials succeed, individualized manufacturing scales with turnaround times and unit costs falling, and intismeran becomes the standard add-on wherever a checkpoint inhibitor is used after surgery (~$40bn end-sales by 2036). The flu and combination vaccines take share in over-50s, the FDA accepts the US combination refiling, and the platform validation carries rare-disease and further oncology assets to market. Margins reach the mid-40s before SBC.
scenario_narratives.bear: Overall survival in melanoma matures without a clear benefit or payers resist a six-figure individualized add-on, the NSCLC trials miss, and intismeran stays a melanoma niche. US vaccine policy narrows COVID and flu eligibility further, RSV stays negligible (it is under $40m a year today), norovirus is dropped, and the section-1498 appeal costs up to $1.3bn. Management reaches cash breakeven by cutting R&D, but at ~$5bn of revenue and a 20% pre-SBC margin the equity is worth little more than the net cash that survives the burn.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Moderna is valued as a cash-burning operating company with a funded path to profitability, where the size of the eventual profit pool depends almost entirely on how far the intismeran result generalises beyond melanoma. The three scenarios are three answers to that question; the respiratory franchise is close to a wash on an owner basis. Every scenario, including bull, values the shares below the current price: the market is capitalising an outcome larger than the bull case modelled here (roughly $15bn+ of annual owner FCF by the mid-2030s, i.e. intismeran economics on the scale of KEYTRUDA itself accruing to Moderna's half). That is a finding about the price, not a reason to stretch the drivers.
key_risks_to_valuation: Intismeran revenue recognition: the model books Moderna's 50% profit-share as half of end-sales with a proportionate cost base. If Merck is principal and Moderna books net profit share, reported revenue is lower and margin higher; owner FCF is the same.
Peak-sales uncertainty is an order of magnitude wide (bear ~$3bn, bull ~$40bn end-sales); NSCLC Phase 3 readouts are the single largest swing and would move the weights, not just the paths.
Individualized manufacturing cost and capacity are unproven at commercial scale; base assumes a ~37% pre-SBC margin at maturity, below large-cap pharma.
SBC is ~19% of revenue and has risen every year since 2022; the paths assume it falls to 6% only because revenue grows 5x.
NOL shelter (~$11-13bn) is modelled as a declining benefit ramping to a 21% cash rate by year 10; faster profitability exhausts it sooner (bull).

The convertible notes are treated as debt at face. Above ~$210.58 they convert into ~14.2m shares (partly offset by capped calls); at the current price that is the relevant treatment and is worth ~3% dilution.
FY0 is a TTM base to 30 Sep 2026; replace with FY2026 actuals and the 31 Dec 2026 balance sheet when the 10-K is filed.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API, regular close at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 22.28-280.80
data_sources.financials: MRNA_Metrics.csv / core_metrics; Form 10-Q for Q3 2026 (balance sheet, cash flow, Notes 11-13, MD&A); Form 10-K FY2025
data_sources.qualitative: Q3-2026 10-Q business highlights and program updates; FY2025 10-K. MRNA_Analysis.json was not yet written at build time.

inputs.share_count_basis: 404m issued and outstanding at 30 Sep 2026 (Q3-2026 10-Q balance sheet) + 24m dilutive equity awards (Q3-2026 EPS note, treasury method). The 14.2m shares underlying the 0.00% 2032 convertible notes are EXCLUDED because the notes are carried as $3.0bn of debt at face (conversion price $210.58 is far above every scenario value; counting both would double-charge). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows.
inputs.sbc_source: Cash-flow-statement add-back, TTM to 30 Sep 2026 = FY2025 483 - 9M-2025 370 + 9M-2026 351 = 464; plus ~7 of tax payments on net share settlement (financing activities, 9M-2026). Moderna publishes no combined adjusted-EBITDA figure, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free ~4.3% (10-yr UST) + ~5% ERP x beta ~1.15 = ~10% cost of equity; debt is a $600m floating term loan and a zero-coupon convertible, too small and too equity-like to lower the blend. 10% in every scenario: pipeline risk is charged through the scenario spread and weights, not through per-scenario discount rates.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment A: operating lease cost stays inside opex (EBITDA); the ~$0.7bn of operating lease liabilities are NOT in net debt. Financing leases are immaterial.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF, 10-year horizon, scenario-weighted (dcf-methods routing: US operating company). The routing table has no risk-adjusted-NPV row; pipeline optionality (intismeran autogene, 50/50 worldwide profit share with Merck) is carried explicitly in the three revenue paths and their weights rather than as a separate rNPV add-on. FY0 is the TRAILING TWELVE MONTHS to 30 Sep 2026 (revenue 1,944 - 1,266 + 1,847 = 2,525), not FY2025, so that the flows start exactly where the 30 Sep 2026 balance sheet stops; year 1 is the 12 months to Sep 2027. Using FY2025 as FY0 would have re-charged nine months of 2026 burn (incl. the $950m Arbutus/Genevant settlement paid July 2026) that the balance sheet has already absorbed. TTM reported FCF -2,044 = OCF -1,785 less PP&E 185 less intangibles 74, and includes the one-off $950m settlement; owner FCF -2,786 after SBC 471 and interest income 271 (stripped because net cash is added in the bridge). Cash 7,976 = cash 1,195 + current investments 3,976 + non-current investments 2,805. Debt 3,600 = term loan 600 + convertible notes at $3,000 face (carrying 2,958). Capped calls (cost $329m) are ignored: out of the money at every scenario value. Moderna is a NON-repurchaser (no buybacks since 2023): the flat share count is a modelling convention the company is not funding. The price rose roughly tenfold from its 52-week low after the positive Phase 3 INTerpath-001 readout (Aug 2026) and ESMO detail (Oct 2026); every scenario value, including bull, sits below the current price -- see valuation_philosophy. No Analysis JSON existed at build time; scenario axes are drawn from the Q3-2026 10-Q and FY2025 10-K.

bear.rationale: Revenue ~4.9bn in year 10: respiratory ~3bn, intismeran melanoma-only (~3bn end-sales, Moderna ~1.5bn), little else. Management cuts to cash breakeven by about year 4 but the business never earns a pharma margin.

base.rationale: Revenue ~12.1bn in year 10 = respiratory/infectious-disease franchise ~4.5bn + Moderna's 50% share of ~14bn intismeran end-sales + ~0.5bn other. Margin is adjusted EBITDA before SBC: TTM is about -52% excluding the settlement (cash costs ~3.85bn on 2.5bn revenue); costs fall to ~3.55bn in year 1 on the R&D wind-downs, then rise with the oncology commercial and manufacturing build to ~7.6bn at maturity. Cash tax is ~nil while ~$11-13bn of post-2022 losses are used, then ramps to 21% by the terminal year so the shelter is not capitalised.

bull.rationale: Revenue ~26.8bn in year 10: intismeran becomes a pan-tumour adjuvant backbone (~40bn end-sales, Moderna's half ~20bn), respiratory ~5.5bn, rare disease and other ~1.5bn. NOLs are consumed by year 6.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (above the 15% default): the equity story now rests on one asset whose survival data are immature and whose larger indications are unread, on top of a US vaccine-policy dependency and an unaccrued $1.3bn litigation tail. Base 50%: melanoma approval is well supported by a replicated Phase 2b/Phase 3 signal, and one NSCLC success is the central expectation. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs several independent Phase 3 trials, manufacturing scale-up and payer acceptance all to go right.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
